title: How the two methods make assignments

name: slide-title
text: How the two methods make assignments

name: greedy-heading
text: Priority-first Greedy

name: greedy-explanation
text:
Critical roles come first, then High, then Normal.

Within each tier, the score adds preferred-skill matches, department preference (+15 / +10 / +5), and experience (+1 per year).

Clear and fast. Earlier choices can limit later matches.

name: ilp-heading
text: PuLP ILP with CBC

name: ilp-explanation
text:
A binary choice represents each eligible person and role slot.

Per filled slot: +100 base; priority adds +50 / +25 / +10. Fit adds up to +10 for preferred skills, +8 / +4 / +2 for department preference, and +0.5 per experience year.

At most one person per slot and one role per volunteer.

name: eligibility-heading
text: Shared eligibility rules

name: eligibility-copy
text: Active account, mandatory skills, event availability, and maximum hours. Vacancies remain open when no eligible person can take them.

name: fairness-gap
text: Current code has no explicit fairness score, and its weights are not centralized.

Sources: backend/app/allocation/greedy.py, ilp_optimizer.py, eligibility.py, and ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md. The code currently hard-codes the stated score additions. The algorithm specification says exact objective weights and a measurable fairness metric remain open; the current ILP objective does not include an explicit fairness term. These implementation weights should not be represented as committee-approved policy.

text: Live demo and production decisions

name: demo-heading
text: Live demo

name: demo-steps
text:
Open http://localhost:5000 and choose the Convener demo account.

Open Reports & Allocation to compare the current snapshot.

Review six open positions, then download the published CSV or Excel roster.

Use the volunteer account to show the personal published-assignment view.

name: decisions-heading
text: Before live deployment

name: production-decisions
text:
Approve and centralize the score weights. Define a measurable fairness policy.

Connect a vetted email provider for volunteer activation.

Use unique secrets and organizer credentials. Keep demo seeding off.

Decide whether department heads need their own authenticated access.

Sources: README.md, PRD.md, ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md, backend/app/services/auth_service.py, and the current web app. Do not place demo passwords in a shareable deck. The login screen has quick demo buttons for the supplied test accounts. Production deployment should use unique organizer credentials, avoid demo seeding, approve the scoring policy, and integrate OTP delivery.
